does: The wait at the end of a game thread's tick: restarts the ls::PreciseClock at +0 of its object, then waits the period at +0x18 less the carry at +0x28 and its second argument (microseconds): while more than 1 ms is left it runs queued ls::WorkerThreadJob items of the worker scheduler's three queues and calls SwitchToThread, the last millisecond a tight QueryPerformanceCounter spin with Sleep(0) every 400 reads; it writes the time measured to +0x20 and how far it overran to +0x28 (the carry the next wait subtracts).

evidence.says: its body: PreciseClock::restart, QueryPerformanceCounter, the 0x3E9 us threshold, the MPMC queue Emplace of WorkerThreadJob, SwitchToThread / Sleep(1) / Sleep(0), and the writes to +0x20 and +0x28

its only caller unplaced::TickLimit calls it when the time since the last tick is within the period; the server's DoWork passes its worker +0x78, whose +0x18 (worker +0x90) is the 33333 us period read live in round 1

questions.ask: the second argument at the one call site (RDX after the floor in unplaced::TickLimit): a probe would show its value
